idiom_note: This product is STATUTE-AS-TEMPLATE. Verified statutory passages form the document's skeleton and the record's facts are woven in against them. Every passage rendered as template must byte-match the provision_texts row its citation names; the citation names the row the bytes actually came from. A passage and its cited row may never be reconciled by editing either the passage or the corpus row.
thesis: Each biometric statute in scope is applied in its own words: the verified passage states the requirement, the practice the record describes is set beside it, and the conclusion is stated first. Where the record is silent, the fact that would settle it is named.

sections.title: The processing as the record describes it
sections.exemplar_after: The record describes fingerprint and palm-print capture from employees at shift start, held by a workforce-management vendor. The record does not say how long the templates are kept.

sections.title: The requirements that attach, and the record against each
sections.exemplar_after: 740 ILCS 14/15(a) requires a private entity in possession of biometric identifiers to develop a written policy, made available to the public, establishing a retention schedule and guidelines for permanently destroying biometric identifiers. The record does not identify such a policy, so the requirement is unmet on the record as supplied.

sections.title: Consent and notice
sections.exemplar_after: A written release is required before collection. The record reports a release executed inside onboarding paperwork; a standalone biometric release is the defensible form.
